sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 45 (quality check 44), Internal Quality Checks row 45 including E45 annotation
evidence: Assigned-row source and arithmetic review only. Workbook Quality Checks!D45 requires real functionality above structure/style; Internal Quality Checks!E45 explicitly describes 60 percent functionality and within-dimension verifier weights. Frozen task tests/scoring.toml:1-11 exactly matches the frozen template: zero-weight gates, functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2, functional floor 0.05. tests/tools/score.py:40-48 applies these weights, normalizes their sum, and yields zero if gates or the strict functional floor fail. Python TOML enumeration found 86 functional criteria with positive weights totaling 45.0, 14 polish criteria totaling 9.0, and 6 visual criteria totaling 6.0. Thus non-functional dimensions contribute at most 0.4, below functionality at 0.6. Functional weights track operational proofs: seven seed rows total only 1/45 of function (0.013333 overall; functional/judge.toml:32-93), versus weight 1 each for actual intrinsic/annualized/run-rate/band-basis/band calculations (:212-255), commitment and grant (:347-363), revision lineage/equity (:392-443), release/cancellation/calendar (:455-497), and authenticated fresh readback (:779-785). Informational feedback weights are 0.25 each (:311-327, :338-345, :410-417); appearance is confined to the six equally weighted visual anchors, while polish owns operability, feedback and recovery. Broken-app challenge: a polished seed-only dashboard cannot satisfy constraints/judge.toml:23-25 because it must create both records and retrieve them in an independent Auditor context; even hypothetically granting only accounts, seed and compensation-view criteria gives 1.75/45 = 0.038889 function, below the floor. Conforming-alternative challenge: a working app with a vertically stacked compensation view, nonmodal forms and native or equivalent accessible roles is expressly accepted by functional/judge.toml:137 and polish/judge.toml:50,59,68,77; no implementation structure or preferred layout is given functional weight. No weight-policy counterexample found. Cited frozen source hashes were recomputed and matched manifest.json, including scoring.toml 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba, score.py 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e, functional judge 9751b2a69b0bb45da61b86828ff967f2737b2ea1fbd088dea97825a851546818, polish judge db23c3a44d06f718e0661a9f6bb8d25eb9508a5a09807902ef3f9554a0e8877e and visual judge 0e465f253a344f47fa60b16bbea1c011fb225fc14a6d35845898b44f66579f33. This static row verdict does not establish configured judge execution, empirical ranking, Oracle/model scores or overall clearance.
